title: Suriya's Vishwanath And Sons Enters Rs 100 Crore Club as Telugu States Outpace Tamil Nadu
excerpt: The family entertainer crossed Rs 100 crore at the Indian box office in 10 days, with Telugu states contributing more than the film's home market — a rare reversal for a Tamil original.
body:
• Vishwanath And Sons, starring Suriya and Mamitha Baiju, crossed Rs 100 crore at the Indian box office within 10 days of its August 14 release.
  • Telugu states (Andhra Pradesh and Telangana) have outperformed Tamil Nadu at the domestic box office — Rs 40.50 crore vs Rs 36.25 crore — a rare reversal for a Tamil-language original.
  • The worldwide gross stands at approximately Rs 174 crore, with Rs 57.50 crore from overseas markets, according to Sacnilk.
  • Director Venky Atluri's family drama has been praised for its progressive writing and sensitive handling of its central premise, drawing strong word-of-mouth across demographics.

A Box Office Milestone in 10 Days

Suriya's latest film Vishwanath And Sons has crossed the Rs 100 crore mark at the Indian box office, reaching the milestone on its second Saturday — just 10 days after its Independence Day release on August 14. The family entertainer, directed by Venky Atluri and produced by Dream Warrior Pictures and Sithara Entertainments, opened to Rs 17.75 crore on its first day and climbed to Rs 26 crore on Saturday and Rs 23.50 crore on Sunday.

https://x.com/NewIndianXpress/status/2091553774116679682

After a weekday slide — Rs 8.50 crore on Monday, tapering to Rs 4.50 crore by Thursday — the film recovered on its second Friday with Rs 4.50 crore, taking its eight-day Indian gross to Rs 95.75 crore. Trade analysts projected the second weekend would push it comfortably past Rs 105 crore.

As of Day 10, the film's India net stands at Rs 100.65 crore, while its worldwide gross has reached approximately Rs 174 crore, including Rs 57.50 crore from overseas markets.

Telugu States Carrying the Film

The most striking feature of Vishwanath And Sons' box-office performance is where the money is coming from. Despite being an original Tamil production, the Andhra Pradesh–Telangana circuit has out-earned Tamil Nadu — Rs 40.50 crore versus Rs 36.25 crore through the first eight days.

This is a rare reversal in south Indian cinema, where regional films typically earn the bulk of their collections in their home-language market. Karnataka contributed Rs 11.50 crore and Kerala added Rs 6.50 crore, while the rest of India accounted for Rs 1.25 crore.

The Telugu version's dominance extended to occupancy as well. On Day 8, the Telugu version contributed Rs 2.35 crore from 1,258 shows at 36% overall occupancy, outperforming the Tamil version. Night shows hit 51% occupancy in Telugu markets.

A Family Story With Depth

Vishwanath And Sons follows Sanjay Vishwanath, an international shooter who has spent his life pursuing excellence and finds his world upended by ageing, family obligations and an unexpected romance. The film has been described as a wholesome family entertainer with progressive writing that handles its central premise with dignity.

"Suriya's charismatic presence and Mamitha Baiju's effortless performance have drawn considerable appreciation from audiences and critics alike."

— Filmfare

The cast also includes Radikaa Sarathkumar and Raveena Tandon. Director Atluri recently revealed that the film's alternate climax was changed at Suriya's suggestion, a detail that has become a talking point among fans.

The makers celebrated the Rs 100 crore milestone at a grand event in Hyderabad attended by the cast and crew. Music by GV Prakash Kumar and cinematography by Nimish Ravi have also drawn praise.

Context in Suriya's Career

Vishwanath And Sons marks a return to form after Suriya's blockbuster Karuppu earlier this year, which grossed significantly more. Trade analyst Pinkvilla noted that while the opening week is strong, it is "underwhelming considering the cost" — the film reportedly carries a production budget of Rs 130 crore, of which it has recovered approximately 60% from domestic theatrical alone.

The film now needs to sustain momentum, particularly with competition from upcoming releases including Toxic.

What's Next

An OTT release date has not been announced. The film continues its theatrical run across Tamil, Telugu, Karnataka and Kerala markets, with the second weekend expected to be decisive for its long-term box-office trajectory.
